speaker: TICKET
text: By eleven, the street outside the house was full of cars. Niggas came in leather. Niggas came in silk. One arrived in a pajama shirt covered with little white moons, a gold chain caught between the buttons. Another still had shaving foam behind his ear. Tank looked at the pajamas.

speaker: TICKET
text: "Nigga, were you asleep?" "I was participating in my relationship." "Well, your relationship open at the bottom." The nigga buttoned himself without slowing down. "Where she at?" "Red's got her," I said. He stopped fixing his shirt. "Aight. What we need?" That was why I'd called. Not because every nigga in that doorway was good.

speaker: TICKET
text: Some would've asked the same question at Red's house if Red had called first. Some had carried T's coffin. Some still owed the women who loved them an answer to a text they'd had time to read six times. But they came. Nigga, I could work with came. The man with shaving foam saw the broken glass. "Red do that?" "I did." "Okay.

speaker: TICKET
text: Nigga, I was about to get separately mad." "Stay with the original mad. We got a deadline." He wiped his ear with his sleeve and went inside. I watched my people fill the room. Bad decisions, borrowed coats, guns, money trouble. A nigga I'd fought six months ago moved a chair so Marcellus could sit more comfortably.

speaker: TICKET
text: Another picked up a shard of glass before Rosa stepped on it. I wanted Shawna back. These were the niggas who had answered. The world could interview better men in the morning. Tank stood at the dining table, putting the three million where everybody could see it. He didn't hide behind me. He waited until the room filled and then he spoke.

speaker: TICKET
text: This is the money from the motel. A few heads turned. I took it. One man beside the piano said, Nigga, what? Tank kept his eyes on the room. I took all of it. I let Aiden think it was gone. Red knew. He tried to use it against him tonight. Tried? somebody asked. Tried. The man beside the piano looked at me.

speaker: TICKET
text: Nigga, and this nigga still breathing? Tank's jaw moved once. I walked between them. Look at me when you say that. The man did. Tank's standing with me. I'm just saying— Say he stole it. He did. Say he's a lying motherfucker. He was. Say you're gonna touch him tonight, and you can find out how fucking fast I can forget your name.

speaker: TICKET
text: The room went still. Tank looked at the back of my head. I could feel it. The man by the piano lifted his hands. Your house. Yeah. I let that sit. My house. My money on the table. My girl with Red. If any of that bothers you, the door already fucking broke. You ain't gotta worry about hurting it. Nobody left.

speaker: TICKET
text: Rosa stood by the staircase in the borrowed coat. She watched every face. Marcellus sat behind her with the decoy in its box and the papers inside his jacket. The old nigga looked tired enough to disappear if you let your eyes move too fast, but he hadn't asked to lie down. I put my hand on the cash.

speaker: TICKET
text: Some of you came because you owe me. Some of you came because Red owes you. Some of you just heard there was gonna be money. One man in the back said, All three. I looked at him. He didn't apologize. I nodded. Good. Nigga knows why he came. I started giving it away. Not throwing it in the air.

speaker: TICKET
text: I wanted every nigga who touched it to look into my face while he did. I wanted him to feel the weight of it and know the woman we'd left behind had carried it out of a room full of killers before any of us had the nerve. Stacks went into hands. Into coats.

speaker: TICKET
text: Into the pajama shirt, where the buttons strained so hard I thought the little moons were gonna fly off. Nigga, put that in a bag, Tank told him. I'm good. You look pregnant. I'm good. I kept paying. Some of them laughed. Some counted.

speaker: TICKET
text: One man held the money without doing either, and I remembered he'd been sitting in a hospital hallway two nights earlier with his head in his hands. Tonight he kissed the stack and tucked it inside his coat. I didn't ask which part of his life I'd just bought. I had one woman to bring home.

speaker: TICKET
text: The whole city could put its heart on the fucking table. When two million had left the bags, I stopped. The last million stayed together. I pulled the bag shut and set it aside. That's hers. Nobody argued. Tank hadn't taken anything. I picked up a share from the two million I'd already laid out and held it toward him. He shook his head. No.

speaker: TICKET
text: Nigga, take it before I have to love you louder. Aiden. Nigga, poor and guilty? I'm letting you have one bad feeling. Pick one. His eyes flicked toward the men around us. Nigga, I don't want it. Then spend it on somebody who does. I pushed the money against his chest until he took it. He looked down at it.

speaker: TICKET
text: Then he put it on the table beside the million I was keeping for Shawna. For her, he said. I left it there. I wasn't counting love back into a fucking bag while everybody watched. Rosa came down the stairs. And before all you niggas start singing about brotherhood, she's my friend. Nobody laughed. They knew her.

speaker: TICKET
text: Half the room stood up straighter when she came close. That means if you see her, you bring her. You don't stop to tell Red how hard you are. You don't start explaining a grudge from 2018. You bring her. The man with shaving foam behind his ear nodded. We got you, Rosa. No, baby. You better have her. She turned to me.

speaker: TICKET
text: I had held back part of the two million for her. I pushed it across the table. She stared at it. What's this? Yours. For what? Whatever you want. Her face went tight. You paying me to stay home? I'm paying you because she loves you. Rosa looked up. Nigga, don't do that right now.

speaker: TICKET
text: She gets out of that car tonight, I want somebody here she knew before every room had me in it. For the first time since she'd walked through the broken door, Rosa looked her age and her fear at once. Thirty-four years old, tired, one earring gone, holding the coat closed with a hand that had finally stopped shaking. You bring her, she said.

speaker: TICKET
text: I nodded. She slapped my face. Not hard enough to knock me down. Hard enough that the room went silent. With your mouth, Aiden. I swallowed. I'm bringing her. She kissed the same cheek. Then go, baby. I turned to the room. Any of you niggas here think Red owns Vegas? Fuck Red, somebody said. Anybody think that nigga owns my wife?

speaker: TICKET
text: Rosa made a sound behind me. I turned halfway. What? You ask her yet? I'm going to. Then quit inviting these niggas before me. The room broke open. Men laughed, slapped each other's shoulders, called out shit about weddings and suits and who wasn't allowed near an open bar. I let them.

speaker: TICKET
text: For a few seconds we had a future big enough to crowd a room. Then I raised my hand. Niggas, listen to me. They quieted. I ain't asking you to die because I fell in love. I'm asking you to stand up with me because that nigga thinks he can take anything he sees. He took a man's wife. Took another man's diamond.

speaker: TICKET
text: Took Dante out to the desert and left him there. Tonight he took Shawna. I put my hand over the cross. He keeps telling everybody I'm wearing a dead nigga's jewelry. Fine. Let him look at it while I come get my girl. Tank stepped beside me. Ten toes, he said. The room answered. Down. He said it again, louder. Ten toes. Down.

speaker: TICKET
text: Nigga, the windows shook. The broken front door moved in its frame. For one wild second I wanted the whole city to hear us, every penthouse and every parking lot and every woman waiting for a man to come back different. I kissed the cross. Then I went outside. Tank drove the Mercedes.

speaker: TICKET
text: I sat beside him because I still couldn't lean back without feeling T's bullet and because if anybody was going to meet Red first, it was going to be me. Marcellus got into the back. I looked over my shoulder. You sure about this? No. Nigga, you can wait with Rosa. I have waited enough.

speaker: TICKET
text: He shut the door before I could offer him anything else. The decoy sat in its box beside him. The letters and the papers were in his coat. My phone lay faceup on my knee. Rosa stood in the driveway with the money she hadn't bothered to pick up still inside the house.

speaker: TICKET
text: Tank had put the bag with Shawna's million and his returned share in the back. Red had asked for three million. He was getting what was left after I'd paid the niggas coming to take his kingdom. She came to my window. Aiden. I looked at her. She likes gardenias. What? For the wedding. She likes gardenias.

speaker: TICKET
text: And she will lie and tell you roses because men always buy roses. I gripped the door. Gardenias. And don't let that old man give her away. I'll do it. Marcellus said, I hadn't volunteered. Rosa pointed at him through the glass. Keep it that way. She stepped back.

speaker: TICKET
text: The cars pulled out behind us until the street looked like the city had emptied its garages for a funeral and nobody had agreed whose. Thirty engines. Maybe more by the time we reached the highway. Rex Crown came in a black coupe; Little Saint rode beside him. Mercedes and Porsche took the green Bentley.

speaker: TICKET
text: Bell had brought my police Lamborghini back, and Knox rode with her at the head of the convoy. Headlights filled both mirrors. My niggas had come wearing their money and their worst intentions, and I loved every last one of them for showing up. Tank kept both hands on the wheel. After a while he said, You should let the doctor look at you after.

speaker: TICKET
text: After. I'm saying. I heard you. He nodded. The lights thinned outside the windows. Vegas went from towers to signs to little burning squares behind us. Ahead was black desert and the road laid through it. Tank. Yeah. When you came back for the money. Did he look like himself? He knew who I meant. He drove another few seconds before he answered. No.

speaker: TICKET
text: I looked down at the cross. Good. Tank's hands tightened. You don't gotta say that. I know. He didn't answer. I watched the side of his face and remembered him standing behind T in the parking lot, as big as a wall, waiting for somebody else to decide what he'd do. I'm glad you here. His jaw moved. Yeah. Don't make me say it twice.

speaker: TICKET
text: I heard you. In the back, Marcellus turned the decoy's box between his hands. She wore blue the last time I took her dancing, he said. Neither of us asked who. Celeste. I was late. She was furious. By the time I got there, she'd danced with three other men. Three? I said. She counted them for me. Tank glanced in the mirror.

speaker: TICKET
text: You do something to those niggas? I asked for the fourth dance. I looked out at the dark. Could've been me. It wasn't. He closed the box and rested his head against the seat. We drove the rest of that stretch without talking. At eleven fifty-four, Red called. I put him on speaker. You coming? he asked. You hear the cars?

speaker: TICKET
text: I told you to come ready to apologize. I am. Tank looked at me. I told her I'd never let you put your hands on her again. Got a lot to apologize for. Red breathed into the phone. You think all those niggas love you? Enough to leave the house. That's money. Then you should've paid better. He went quiet.

speaker: TICKET
text: I heard Shawna in the background. I couldn't make out the words, only her voice and the way he moved the phone away from her. Let me talk to her. You'll see her soon. Nigga, let me— He hung up. I gripped the phone so hard Tank reached over and took it before I broke that too. We're here, he said.

speaker: TICKET
text: The casino rose out of the desert half finished, huge and white under lights that made the empty windows look blacker. Red had built columns tall enough for a king and stopped before anybody could decide what kingdom he thought he had. Plastic sheeting moved behind the glass. A fountain outside had never held water. Cars waited across the entrance. Men stood between them.

speaker: TICKET
text: Above the front doors, a balcony ran along the second floor beneath an unfinished crown of stone. There she was. Shawna stood at the railing in Rosa's ruined dress. Her hair blew across her face. Even from the car I could see Dante's watch on her wrist. Red stood beside her.

speaker: TICKET
text: He lifted the hand with the ring and waved like he'd invited us for dinner. Behind me, engine after engine went quiet. My niggas were here. I opened my door. My side hurt. My hand hurt. Everything in me that knew how to be scared was awake and screaming. I put both feet on the ground anyway. Shawna saw me.

speaker: TICKET
text: She stepped toward the railing before Red caught her arm. Aiden! I looked straight up at her. I'm here, baby. The clock on my phone turned eleven fifty-nine. The first roadblock waited beyond the last gas station. Two trucks across the highway. Men beside them. No uniforms. No lights except the white glare of their headlights pointed into our faces.

speaker: TICKET
text: A line of barrels burned between the trucks, and behind the flames I could see the same kind of patience Red had worn across the breakfast table. Tank slowed. Behind us thirty engines changed their voices at once. My phone rang. Knox. "I see them," she said.

speaker: TICKET
text: "Stay in the convoy." "Nigga, the convoy is me." "Then don't make me explain to your wife why you turned into a road accident before you got there." A shot hit the Mercedes hood. Tank pulled left. Another struck the windshield and made a white star directly in front of him.

speaker: TICKET
text: Marcellus dropped in the back, his coat closed over the letters and the decoy like the old nigga had decided history could wait below the window line. Knox's police Lamborghini came out beside us. Officer Bell was driving; the chief leaned forward in the passenger seat, looking at the roadblock like somebody had finally annoyed her enough to deserve the whole department. The siren rose.

speaker: TICKET
text: One of the men by the truck stepped backward. Another raised his gun anyway. "Hardheaded nigga," I said. Tank put his foot down. We left the road in a sheet of dust. The Mercedes bounced across the shoulder, hit a shallow ditch, and came up with its engine still screaming. My head struck the roof. I tasted blood.

speaker: TICKET
text: Behind us the convoy divided, cars sweeping wide through the desert while shots flashed between the trucks. The men had expected a line. They got a fucking horizon. Rex's black coupe came past on our right. Little Saint rode beside it on a new motorcycle with no paint on the tank.

speaker: TICKET
text: He'd borrowed it from a man who apparently understood lending something to my nigga meant accepting an interesting return policy. Mercedes and Porsche came through the dust in the green Bentley. Porsche had the roof down. Mercedes held her hair away from her face with one hand and a pistol in the other. "Keep the old man down!" she shouted as they passed.

speaker: TICKET
text: "Old man is down," Marcellus said from the back seat. "The old man is thoroughly fucking down." I couldn't help it. I laughed. Nigga, I laughed with a bullet hole in my windshield and the woman I loved waiting inside a nightmare, because that old man had come through eight years of prison and still knew when my friends needed correcting.

speaker: TICKET
text: The first truck started moving. Its driver turned toward the desert to cut off the cars passing on that side. Rex braked hard. Little Saint swerved clear. The truck's huge front wheel climbed the edge of a ditch, and for a second the whole thing leaned toward the coupe. I saw Rex looking up through his windshield. I saw Little Saint turn back.

speaker: TICKET
text: "Tank." "I see." "Nigga, this time I believe you." Tank drove the Mercedes straight into the truck's rear corner. Metal struck metal. The car jumped sideways. My shoulder hit the door, and every stitch in my side tried to leave without me. The truck's rear swung away from Rex, its wheels clawing at loose dirt. It rolled far enough that the coupe could get clear.

speaker: TICKET
text: Little Saint rode through the gap beside it and came out raising one fist. "Aiden!" "Tank!" I shouted back. The big nigga glanced at me. "What?" "I'm giving you your fucking credit. Enjoy it." He grinned despite the blood on his lip. The truck stopped against a low rise.

speaker: TICKET
text: Its driver jumped out, took one look at the number of cars now surrounding him, and dropped the gun he'd brought down from the cab. Bell and Knox reached him first. The chief got out with her weapon raised. "You blocked my captain's road." The man stared at the gold on her uniform. "Your captain?" She pointed toward me through the dust.

speaker: TICKET
text: "That one." He looked. His face fell so completely I almost respected the honesty of it. "They didn't say it was him." "Nigga," I shouted from the window, "what part of thirty cars looked like a small mistake?" Rex pulled beside us with his window down. His eyebrow was still bleeding where the gala guard had hit him. He looked at Tank, then at me.

speaker: TICKET
text: "Three times." "That one was Tank." "Then I owe the family." Tank lifted two fingers off the wheel. The nigga didn't even try to look modest. I'd have been angry if he had. Behind us, Knox's officers took the men off the road. The second truck's crew had run before the first one stopped moving.

speaker: TICKET
text: I could see their flashlights bouncing through the distance, four little dots trying to become somebody else's fucking problem. The convoy found the highway again. Thirty engines. A few more scratched. A few more loud. Nobody missing. The police Lamborghini took the front while Knox's remaining cruisers held the road behind us.

speaker: TICKET
text: Bell gave the siren one short burst, and the cars answered with their horns. Marcellus sat up carefully in the back. "Are we finished doing that?" "For now." "Good. My tie has given up." I reached back and straightened it for him at the next slow bend. "Nigga, you meeting forty million dollars. Look ready." He looked at me, then down at the cross.

speaker: TICKET
text: "Damn, boy," he said. I smiled. "Magnificent." The old man nodded as if he'd completed the last repair the evening required. At eleven fifty-nine, the unfinished casino rose out of the desert in front of us. Lights burned behind its empty windows. Our headlights spread across the parking lot until every naked wall had a shadow of my people on it.

speaker: TICKET
text: I saw blue on a balcony. Shawna. My whole fucking body knew before my eyes finished the distance. Tank stopped the Mercedes. I opened the door.
